approaches.name: ICT-based TVET voucher MIS for provider payments and beneficiary tracking
approaches.description: An internet-based TVET voucher MIS handles applications, assessment verification and provider payments, tracking beneficiaries for results-based disbursement. Practices: ICT-based TVET voucher with internet MIS tracking beneficiaries; TVET Voucher System tracking providers and beneficiaries for DLI payments.
approaches.why_innovative: New process: ICT-based voucher application, verification and payment - cue: 'voucher mechanism' | category Financial; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The project will adopt the voucher mechanism under the existing Ghana TVET Voucher Project to train apprentices and master craft persons, using training providers.

extra_evidence.text: The financing mechanism includes an internet-based MIS, which tracks individual beneficiaries and monitors their progress and performance.
Specifically, the application process for the program, the assessment verification process, and the payment process are all ICT based.

Year 1 refers to the Government’s fiscal year 2021. • Formalized, standardized, and quality-assured apprenticeship training refers to competency-based training as certified by COTVET, consistent with the country’s NTVETQF, and using the existing Ghana TVET Voucher Project’s system to provide payments to training providers and beneficiaries and to track the status, progress, and performance of providers and beneficiaries.

Evidence for verification of achievement • All training providers (including master craft persons) and beneficiaries will be assigned unique identification numbers. • The unique identification number is to be used in all relevant documentation and data related to the provider or beneficiary. • Data obtained from the TVET Voucher System, or any other component specific MIS, covering records on payments to training providers and beneficiaries and individual-level information on baseline characteristics, eligibility indicators, and training status, progress, and performance, including dates for entry/enrollment and exit/completion in relation to training. • Official accounting records of payments to providers and beneficiaries. • Samples of scanned certificates of enrollment and completion of training by individuals (including by master craft persons). • From project year 2, survey-based independent verification of training receipt status of a sample drawn from relevant data obtained from the TVET Voucher System or any other component specific MIS.

sector.rationale: TVET voucher mechanism directly supports vocational training delivery and payment.

approaches.name: Linked labor market and TVET information systems with offline and assistive access
approaches.description: GLMIS links TVMIS, Artisan Directory and Jobs Center databases, with offline capability and assistive technologies, while TVMIS and STI MIS track sector performance. Practices: GLMIS labor market information system with offline and assistive access; GLMIS labor market information system linked to agency databases; TVMIS and STI MIS sector performance tracking systems.
approaches.why_innovative: New service: integrated labor market information platform with offline and disability access - cue: 'operationalization' | category Technological; adoption apply; judged in 1 round(s); final check: digital core, in_use before 2019

evidence.text: The project will finance the development, operationalization, and maintenance of the GLMIS.

extra_evidence.text: (e) Development of offline capabilities for use in locations with no internet connectivity;

(h) Connection between the GLMIS and other relevant Government databases or MISs that capture information on skills development and jobs, such as the Artisan Directory Platform and the Jobs Center of the Youth Employment Agency, and the Technical and Vocational Management Information System (TVMIS) of COTVET, and with private online job portals;
To support overall labor market information collection and use, the Government will fully develop, operationalize, maintain, and use the GLMIS managed by MELR.
Relevant management information systems and databases managed by other ministries and agencies will be linked to the GLMIS.
These databases include the Artisan Directory Platform and Jobs Center of the Youth Employment Center, and the TVMIS of COTVET.

Project funds, through Component 4, are also made available for the procurement of goods and services to strengthen (a) the TVMIS managed by COTVET, which aims to capture key status, progress, and performance information on the entire TVET sector, including apprenticeship training and (b) an STI MIS managed by MESTI, which aims to capture key status, progress, and performance information on Page 41 of 102 The World Bank Ghana Jobs and Skills Project (P166996) science, technology, and innovation (STI) entities and activities in the country.
Currently, the TVMIS is in an early stage of development while the STI MIS is in an early stage of conceptualization.
